basic_identification.full_title: Food for Special Medical Purpose Intended for Infants — Specification
basic_identification.sector_category: Food and Agriculture (approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Dairy Products and Equipment Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard prescribes the types, requirements, methods of test, and sampling for food for special medical purpose intended for infants (specifically preterm infant milk substitutes, lactose free infant milk substitutes, and hypoallergenic infant milk substitutes). These are formulated as substitutes for human milk or infant formula to meet the specialized nutritional requirements of infants from birth to twenty-four months with specific disorders, diseases, or medical conditions under dietary management.

certification_and_marking.disclaimer: The standard text indicates that certification is permissive: conforming products 'may be certified' and 'may be marked' with the BIS Standard Mark under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. However, the standard mandates strict nutritional limits, detailed diagnostic warning labels, mandatory medical supervision statements, and sets environmental consent guidelines for obtaining the voluntary ECO-Mark.

requirements.provision: The products conforming to the requirements of this standard may be certified under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016, and marked with the Standard Mark.
An advisory warning stating 'RECOMMENDED TO BE TAKEN UNDER MEDICAL ADVICE ONLY' must be conspicuously printed in bold and capital letters on the primary container label.

Packaging must bear the explicit warnings: 'Infant milk substitute is not the sole source of nourishment of an infant' and clear, detailed instructions for appropriate, hygienic preparations to prevent health hazards.

Formula-specific designations must be clearly printed in bold and capital letters: 'FOR THE PRETERM BABY (BORN BEFORE 37 WEEKS)' for preterm substitutes; 'LACTOSE-FREE' for lactose intolerant options; and 'CONTAINS NO MILK OR MILK PRODUCTS' if the formula is devoid of milk derivatives.

To carry the optional ECO-Mark, the manufacturer must produce official consent clearances under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, Water Cess Act, 1977, and Air Act, 1981, and the product must carry the BIS Standard Mark for quality.
All manufacturing, raw ingredients, and packaging remain subject to the strict statutory restrictions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Infant Milk Substitutes (IMS) Act, 1992.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 17945:2022 is the national Indian Standard specification governing Food for Special Medical Purpose (FSMP) intended for infants from birth to twenty-four months with specific diseases, disorders, or medical conditions. It classifies products into three key types: preterm, lactose-free, and hypoallergenic infant milk substitutes. While utilizing IS 14433 and IS 15757 as baseline nutritional reference frames, this code regulates specific compositional deviations required to manage target medical conditions safely. When selecting or auditing these clinical formulas, developers must verify strict compliance with specific micro-nutrient limits (such as DHA, Arachidonic acid, and vitamins), verify low scorched particle thresholds, confirm that microbiological parameters meet the detailed 2-class or 3-class sampling criteria, and ensure that mandatory medical supervision warnings are boldly displayed on all product packaging.
